newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia rice exports to soar in 96/97 - ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia rice exports to soar in 96/97 - ABARE.

text.p: Australian (paddy) rice exports were forecast to jump by 71 percent in the year to June 30, 1997 although average grower returns were set to dip, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said.
In its December quarter bulletin, ABARE forecast exports to rise to 816,000 tonnes in 1996/97 compared to a forecast of 717,000 in its September quarter survey.

The average return to Australian rice growers was forecast to fall 7.2 percent to A$192 per tonne of paddy rice reflecting lower world prices and the prospect of having to discount more heavily to dispose of a much larger harvest, the agency said.

"Nevertheless, returns to Australian rice growers remain favourable and, with abundant supplies of irrigation water assured, rice plantings are forecast to reach a record 165,000 hectares in 1996/97, 16,000 more than 1995/96," ABARE said.

"Australian rice production in 1996/97 is forecast to be a record 1.45 million tonnes (paddy), 53 percent higher than in 1995/96 when yields were adversely affected by cool weather in early 1996," ABARE said.
World prices were forecast to decline slightly under the pressure of increased supplies and lower prices for other food grains, particularly wheat.
